item.title: “Alright, morv?” Increasing the use of our unique language in every day life
item.description: IF Islanders see the word ‘Grève’ most will think ‘beach’. They may also bid someone farewell with a cheery ‘À bétôt’. Some may also describe their broken bike or phone as ‘foutu’. If they do, they are speaking – either consciously or unconsciously – Jèrriais and are using words that are unique to the Island. item.title: Call for reform of work permit system which has “elements of modern day slavery”
item.description: A REFORM Jersey politician has demanded reform to Jersey’s work permit system, warning it is trapping migrant workers in conditions with “elements of modern day slavery”.
